standard_prerequisites.name: The product structure of the graph on the coordinate subsets, and the isoperimetric inequality on sub-products
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's displayed inequalities at source lines 223-226, delivered as a context span of this card
standard_prerequisites.use: Bounds the number of edges a set must cross when it separates a sub-product, which is the mechanism of the counting argument.

standard_prerequisites.name: The relation between the number of coordinates, the dimension parameter d and the order n of the graph
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's preliminaries and proof outline (source lines 201-240)
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the choice m = log_2(log^5 d) into the numerical bound exp(2a/log d).

core_obligations: Choose the slice: set m = log_2(log^5 d) and consider the sub-product G(I,v) obtained by fixing the coordinates outside a set I of size m; a set with a small boundary must intersect non-trivially with at most a log^2 d / t of these sub-products (proof lines 721-726).

Apply the isoperimetric inequality on a sub-product: if A meets a sub-product non-trivially then that sub-product spans at least m edges of the boundary, which is what limits the number of sub-products the set can meet (proof line 726).

Count the admissible choices: the author bounds the number of sets meeting few sub-products by the product of two binomial coefficients, choosing first the sub-products contained in A and then the remaining vertices (proof lines 727-730).
Evaluate the bound and optimise: using a >= n/d^{log^2 d} the author evaluates the binomial product, sums over the choices of I and obtains the stated exp(2a/log d) (proof lines 731-742).
proof_roadmap: 先固定一个 m = log2(log^5 d) 个坐标的切片，把集合在子乘积上的相交次数压到 a log^2 d / t 以内：只要与某个子乘积非平凡相交，该子乘积就至少贡献 m 条边界边。
再用两个二项式系数（先选被包含的子乘积、再选其余顶点）控制候选集合个数，代入 a >= n/d^{log^2 d} 并对 I 求和，得到 exp(2a/log d)。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the counting lemma for large sets with a small edge boundary (author lemma at source lines 714-716, label lem:small-boundary-sets): for a in the stated range, at most exp(2a/log d) sets of size a have an edge boundary below a log^2 d. The proof (source lines 718-743) has genuine content: it restricts to a sub-product on a set I of m = log_2(log^5 d) coordinates, applies the author's isoperimetric inequality on that sub-product to force any set with a small boundary to interact non-trivially with few of the fibres, converts that into a binomial-product bound on the number of admissible sets, and then optimises over m and over the choice of I to reach the exponential bound (proof lines 719-742). The lemma is one of the two counting inputs to the size bound on obstructions. H2.
